companyName: City of San Marcos Public Services Complex
rationale: Archive the City of San Marcos Public Services Complex from the active North American PortCo list and retire the unsupported Amber ownership period. City records identify Hunt San Marcos Development, LLC as a third-party developer and document a ground lease and acquisition agreement under which the City would purchase the completed facility for up to $44.4 million. Hunt's releases describe Amber and Hunt as the development and financing team under a Progressive Development Agreement; they do not disclose continuing direct equity ownership. The City completed the facility in October 2021 and now uses it for municipal operations. No current Amber portfolio listing, direct equity disclosure, continuing concession, or post-completion ownership evidence was found. Because a direct Amber ownership period is not established, no exit year is invented.

beforeImage.name: City of San Marcos Public Services Complex
beforeImage.description: The City of San Marcos Public Services Complex is a municipal accommodation project developed for the City of San Marcos, Texas. The facility supports city operations through a long-term availability-based public-private partnership structure rather than direct demand risk. Public sponsor materials describe the project as a roughly 155,000 square foot complex consolidating multiple public service departments. Amber Infrastructure and Hunt closed financing in 2020 and the city opened the facility in 2021. Reviewed public sources do not disclose the current ownership percentages between the sponsor parties.

afterImage.name: City of San Marcos Public Services Complex
afterImage.description: The City of San Marcos Public Services Complex is a municipal facilities project in San Marcos, Texas. Hunt San Marcos Development, LLC was selected as the third-party developer; the City authorized a ground lease and acquisition agreement with a facility purchase price of up to $44.4 million, and the Amber-Hunt team achieved financial close in September 2020 under a Progressive Development Agreement. The City completed the complex in October 2021 and opened it the following month. Reviewed primary sources establish Amber's development and financing role but do not establish a current direct equity interest, so the record is excluded from the active PortCo list.
